decision_rule: Open a follow-up only if both of these hold: same-fact pairs with both partners packed take at least 5% of packed tokens on average; and in some similarity band, at least 95% of the labeled pairs are the same fact once pairs that differ in a number, a date or a negation are set aside. A follow-up would fold such pairs at packing time only and keep both claims and their evidence in the store. If either condition fails, close the issue with the numbers. (#255)
reading: Packed tokens are the packer's own count of the whole rendered context (MemoryBundle.tokens_used, the gate's context_tokens) with the configured tokenizer. A packed record's tokens are the token_cost the packer charged for its rendered line, with the same tokenizer. At a threshold, a packed claim counts when at least one claim paired with it at or above the threshold is packed in the same context; its share is taken per question and averaged over every replayed question. The upper bound counts every such pair as the same fact. The adjusted estimate counts each pair with the labeled same-fact rate of its sampling band, and a claim with several packed partners with the chance that at least one of them is the same fact, as if pairs were independent. Condition 1 reads the adjusted estimate for all pairs at or above 0.90. Condition 2 reads each sampling band ([0.90, 0.95), [0.95, 0.97) and [0.97, 1.00]) on its own labeled pairs, after different-fact pairs that differ only in a number, a date or a negation are set aside. Pairs whose texts are identical after normalization count like any other pair. The report also applies the rule under the readings this does not use (the upper bound, pooled tokens, the records' own tokens as the denominator, the 'at or above' bands weighted by their pair counts, and both conditions with identical-text pairs set aside), and names any that would change the decision.
labeling_rule: Same fact: both records state the same proposition about the same subject: one event or occurrence, state, attribute, relationship, preference or plan. Wording, word order, a name in place of I, hedges and filler do not matter, and neither does the date a line shows when both dates refer to the same occurrence or state. A record that says everything the other says and adds detail is still the same fact, because the other line adds nothing beside it. Where a line leaves a reference open (it, that, there), the claim's subject, predicate and object and its source turn decide what it refers to. Different facts: each record states something the other does not: another event, or the same kind of event on another occasion; another object, attribute, person, place, amount, time or polarity; or a detail on each side that the other lacks. A different-fact pair is also marked with the one thing that alone separates it, if there is one: number (the same proposition with another count or amount), date (the same kind of event or statement on another date or occasion) or negation (one record denies what the other asserts).

decision.outcome: close the issue with the numbers
